what: Mix architecture: how the pump (sidechain) is made and how deep, how the parts are grouped into buses, what sits on the master. production is a patch merged into the style's production recipe (pump targets and depth: full, deep, medium or depth_db; buses). The measured pump depth of each demo's loudest section (synth band, dB over a beat) is in docs/DEMO_STUDY.md.

options.label: Deep pump on music and bass (volume shaper from the kick)
options.what: Every kick ducks the music and the bass hard and they swell back before the next beat: the house and techno breath, made with a Balance volume clip following the kick.

sources.where: Basic Sidechain (Fruity Envelope Controller) triggered on every beat
GHOST kick channel as the sidechain trigger

options.label: Gentle pump, only on pads and bass
options.what: A shallow duck (about 6 dB) on the sustained parts only, so the vocal and the drums stay steady: pop dance, afro house and liquid records breathe without pumping.

sources.where: Peak Controller from the kick to the bass and synths, Love Philter preset Sidechain

options.label: No pump: space by arrangement and EQ
options.what: Nothing ducks: the bass avoids the kick by its rhythm, the low end is carved by EQ. Drill, trap, lo-fi, trip hop and soundtrack records sound wrong pumped.

sources.where: no sidechain: Beat Bus with a Soft Clipper
one hall reverb for everything, no pump

options.label: Ghost-trigger pump: the pulse without a kick
options.what: A silent trigger channel (a ghost kick or a Sytrus note) drives the sidechain on its own rhythm, so the music keeps pumping where the kick is out (breakdowns, intros) or pumps on a pattern the kick does not play: 'just the pulse behind the pump'.
options.manual: pump_source ghost: the pump follows a four-on-the-floor grid through every section, not the kick's own hits.

options.label: Gross Beat volume gate on bass and chords
options.what: A rhythmic volume shape (Gross Beat) chops the held bass and chords in 8ths or 16ths: a pump that is also a rhythm, independent of the kick.

sources.where: GROSS BEAT on the Saw Bass, Volume Duck Balance

options.manual: Put Gross Beat on the bass insert with a 1/8 volume gate; the engine's pump stands in until it is set.

options.label: Sidechain bus: kick and snare gate a limiter on the music
options.what: Kick and snare feed a 'SC' bus that drives sidechained limiters on pads, bass and chords (Fruity Limiter's compressor keyed from the bus): the music ducks on the backbeat as well as the kick, a hip-hop and lo-fi pump.

sources.where: SC bus fed by kick and snare, Limiter sidechain gates on the music
SC bus: Limiter Transients and Hard Noise Gate presets, keyed into pads, bass and chords

options.manual: Route kick and snare to a bus with no output, key Fruity Limiter (compressor mode) on the music bus from it.

options.label: The vocal ducks the music
options.what: A Peak Controller on the vocal turns the lead synths and the vocal reverb down while the singer sings, so a busy drop can carry a vocal; the reverb is gated by Gross Beat so it never smears the next line.

sources.where: Main Vocal chain ends in Fruity Peak Controller; Vocal Reverb: Reeverb 2 > Gross Beat Gate > Balance (Reverb Sidechain)

options.manual: Peak Controller on the vocal insert linked to the Lead Group Balance volume (inverted), about 4 dB of reduction.

options.label: Full bus tree with one global reverb
options.what: Every family on its bus (All Drums, Sfx, Chromatics, Bass, Synths, Pads), the music buses into All Music, everything into a Mix Buss before the master, one global reverb send shared by all: glue by structure.

sources.where: buses All Drums, Sfx, Chromatics, Bass, Synths, Pads, All Music, Mix Buss and a global Verb send

options.label: Beat bus with a soft clipper
options.what: Drums and melody summed into a Beat Bus that hits a soft clipper before the master, the vocal buses beside it: the beat is loud and dense, the vocal sits on top untouched.

sources.where: Beat Bus (Fruity Soft Clipper) fed by Melody Bus and Drum Bus; vocal buses and REVERB, 1/4 DELAY, 1/2 DELAY sends

options.manual: Fruity Soft Clipper on the drum bus at about 2 dB of clipping.

options.label: One hall for everything
options.what: A single bright hall (LuxeVerb, 3 s) as the only reverb, every instrument sent to it at its own level: one room, a cinematic and acoustic sound.

sources.where: Reverb bus: LuxeVerb Bright Hall 3 Sec Decay fed by every instrument

options.manual: create_send_route from each music insert to one reverb insert with LuxeVerb.

options.label: Master: mid-side EQ, hard clip, limiter
options.what: A master chain that shapes the mid and side separately, then clips the peaks (WaveShaper hard clip) before a transparent limiter: loud and punchy without pumping the limiter.

sources.where: Master: Patcher (Mid | Side EQ) > EQ (MakeUp) > WaveShaper (Hard Clip) > Emphasis Limiter

options.manual: apply_club_master with the style's targets does the loudness; this names the chain to prefer.

options.label: Mono low end, wide top, the bass ducked hard
options.what: Everything under 150 Hz in mono (side 35 dB under mid), the hats and the top wide (side 3 dB under mid above 4 kHz), the bass and music ducked 12 to 15 dB by every kick and back within about 90 ms: a club mix that stays solid on mono systems.

sources.where: side minus mid below 150 Hz -35 to -38 dB (the record: -13 dB), above 4 kHz -3 dB; bass envelope -10 to -15 dB at each kick, full again by the off-beat

options.manual: Fruity Stereo Shaper or a mid-side EQ low-cut on the side below 150 Hz on the master or the bass bus.

options.label: Pump with an exponential recovery: silent on the hit, back fast, easing in
options.what: The music bus and bass drop fully on each kick, hold for about a tenth of a beat, then come back on a curve: most of the way within the next tenth of a beat, easing into full level by 0.3 beat. Clicks less than a straight ramp and pumps harder on the first 16th.
options.how: The person's Red Lights breakdown: silence for 40 ms, about -3 dB at 100 ms, full by about 140 ms at 125 bpm (gain 1 - e^(-(t-40)/50)). pump.pump_points with curve exp.

sources.where: the person's breakdown: the synth bus ducking curve, -inf for 40 ms, recovered by about 140 ms
